# COMMONHOUR — complete client room and object records

## Project

- Product: COMMONHOUR.
- Household: two adults, A and B, renting their home.
- Furniture system: one complete freestanding expandable table with internal storage.
- States: W, D and S.
- Fixed conversion-board wording: Work away, dinner ready.
- Image-title and document-cover identity: COMMONHOUR followed by the relevant role or state.
- Native room drawings: room-plan.png and room-elevations.png; shared empty-room geometry.
- Dimension unit: millimetres unless stated otherwise.

## Room coordinates and fixed areas

| Room depth | y=0–3000, entrance wall to rear wall |
| Room height | z=0–2600, finished floor to flat ceiling |
| Main circulation strip | x=0–3600, y=0–900; clear of fixed, parked and stored furniture and objects |
| Movement through circulation strip | A person or carried part during an identified movement |
| Existing low cabinet | x=0–1200, y=2600–3000, z=0–700; solid occupied volume |
| Work-kit storage destination | Internal table storage |

| Window opening | y=1400–2600, z=900–2100 |

## Household schedule and states

| A and B | Dining together, 19:00–20:00 |
| W | One active workplace for A; L/K/M/N on the surface; F/C in internal storage |
| D | Two simultaneous dining places for A and B; all six work items concealed inside the table |
| S | Complete assembled table stored between uses; all six work items concealed inside the table |

## Existing chairs

| Chair IDs | CH-A and CH-B |
| Quantity | 2 |

| D chair arrangement | Both chairs active; empty parking area available for passage |
| S chair arrangement | Both chairs in the reserved parking area; table outside that area |
| Chair status | Existing household objects |

## Work and dining envelopes

| Record | Fixed value |

| W clear surface | At least 1000 long × 600 deep |
| W surface height | 720–760 |
| W simultaneous surface objects | Open L, K, M and N |
| W internal objects | F and C |
| D clear surface | At least 1200 long × 800 deep |
| D surface height | 720–760 |
| D place-setting areas | 2 separate areas, each 600 × 400 |
| Plates | 2, each diameter 240 |
| Cups | 2, each diameter 80 × 100 high |
| Setting positions | Within the two place-setting areas |
| Each active chair floor-use envelope | 600 wide × 900 deep, measured outward from its table edge |
| Chair depth within use envelope | 500 |
| Active-chair envelope location | Within the room, outside the main circulation strip and protected window band |
| Associated under-table leg space | Clear of table supports |

## Complete work-item inventory

| ID | Item | Quantity | Closed or stored envelope | W condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L | Laptop | 1 | 330 × 230 × 20 | Base 330 × 230 on the surface; open screen rises nominally 220 above the rear base edge |
| K | Keyboard | 1 | 280 × 120 × 20 | On the surface |
| M | Mouse | 1 | 120 × 70 × 40 | On the surface |
| N | Notebook | 1 | 210 × 297 × 18 | Closed notebook on the surface |
| F | Folder | 1 | 320 × 240 × 40 | In internal storage |
| C | Cable box | 1 | 180 × 120 × 70 | Closed box containing loose cables, in internal storage |

- Complete kit quantity: exactly 6 named items.
- Item geometry: listed dimensions and separate identities retained; rotation available.
- L storage condition: closed.
- D and S storage: all 6 items inside actual table compartments, with allocated volumes and access paths.
- W storage: F and C inside the table.
- Electronics arrangement: self-contained work kit; cables contained in C.

## Stored envelope and component continuity

- S maximum assembled envelope: 1100 long × 600 deep × 850 high, including handles, supports and the complete stored work kit.
- W, D and S component basis: the same actual furniture parts.
- Principal assemblies, removable leaves, trays, supports and hardware pouch: stable designer-selected IDs.
- Ordinary individual fasteners: grouped quantities available in the component inventory.
- Conversion accounting: a stated location for every component throughout movement.
- W-to-D locations: all removed pieces and work objects remain in the room and reach their allocated final locations.
- Furniture movement: available within the permitted room areas, with positions recorded in the sequence.
- Product quantity: one table integrating work, dining and storage.

## Materials and actual connections

| Supports | Powder-coated steel tube |

| Grips and transformation hardware | Designer selection, recorded by actual component |
| Relocation fasteners | M6 bolts with captive nuts |
| Relocation tool | 4 mm hex key |
| Relocation fastener quantity | Designer selection, recorded with the assembly inventory |
| Transformation connection | Actual expanding or converting joint, with operation, support and retention identified |
| Separation connection | Actual joint for separating and reassembling the table for moving, with operation, support and retention identified |
| Connection detail count | At least 2 meaningful details; shared hardware possible where both functions are explained |

## Relocation records

| Record | Fixed value |

| Furniture preparation | Folding and/or separation into named modules |
| Work-kit preparation | All 6 items removed from the table and packed together |
| Client tote envelope | 400 × 320 × 180 |
| Each principal furniture module | At most 1300 × 850 × 250 in a stated packing orientation, including protrusions |
| Small hardware | 1 identified pouch, accounted for with the modules |
| Handling participants | 2 adults, with proposed holding and support positions |
| Moving sequence | Room doorway, outside turning square, rightward corridor |
| Available orientations | Flat, tilted or upright, with the chosen orientation recorded |
| Moving demonstration contents | Table modules, hardware pouch and work-kit tote |
| Existing chairs and cabinet | Remain outside the moving sequence |

## Same-room application cases

| Case | Time | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| W1 | 10:00 | A working; L/K/M/N on the surface; F/C inside; CH-B parked |
| D1 | 19:00 | A and B dining; all 6 work items inside |
| S1 | Between uses | Assembled stored table and both parked chairs; stored-state location key |

- Application setting: the same room in all cases.
- Additional-view subjects: alternate camera, reverse conversion, enlarged actual connections, item retrieval and the same moving turn.
- Shared design records across views: table modules, geometry, item counts and chosen materials.

steps.userMessage:
COMMONHOUR | One rental-home table for work, dinner and moving day

We are commissioning COMMONHOUR, an expandable table with internal storage for a renting household of two adults, A and B. A works from 09:00 to 17:00; B returns at 18:30, and they dine together from 19:00 to 20:00. The table has three states: W, one active workplace; D, two simultaneous dining places; and S, the assembled table stored between uses. W needs a clear surface of at least 1000 × 600 mm, D at least 1200 × 800 mm, both at a height of 720–760 mm. D contains two separate 600 × 400 mm place-setting areas. The complete S envelope, including handles and the stored work kit, is at most 1100 × 600 × 850 mm. The expansion method and silhouette are open. Develop the states from the same identifiable assemblies, with a location for every part throughout conversion.

The room is 3600 × 3000 × 2600 mm. Its entrance-side circulation strip is 900 mm deep; the cabinet, chair parking, door swing and protected window band are fixed in the attached room records. Each active chair needs a 600 × 900 mm floor-use envelope. The household keeps chairs CH-A and CH-B and six work items: laptop L, keyboard K, mouse M, notebook N, folder F and cable box C. In W, L/K/M/N are on the surface and F/C are inside; in D and S, all six are concealed inside the table. Use 18 mm birch plywood with clear water-based lacquer for the tabletop and storage panels, and powder-coated steel tube for the supports. Relocation connections use M6 bolts with captive nuts, operated with a 4 mm hex key; select and record their quantity. Each separated furniture module fits within 1300 × 850 × 250 mm in its packing orientation. The moving route passes through an 800 × 2050 mm doorway, a 900 × 900 mm turning square and a 900 mm-wide corridor. Print "COMMONHOUR" in every image title and on every document cover, followed by the relevant role or state. Print "Work away, dinner ready" on the conversion and storage board.

Audience: the furniture studio and its workshop partner, choosing a table for renters who share limited space between home working and dining and need to take the same furniture to their next home.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the household schedule, room coordinates, object inventory, use envelopes and furniture requirements. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverable proportions, formats and stages. room-plan.png is the constraint drawing for the room boundary, circulation, door swing, cabinet, chair parking and moving route. room-elevations.png is the constraint drawing for the entrance and window heights. household-objects.png is the identity board for the household's existing work kit and dining objects. morning-room.png is an atmosphere reference for A's working day in this room. evening-room.png is an atmosphere reference for A and B preparing to eat in the same room.

Deliverables:
1. Three finished state drawings, one each for W, D and S, with dimensioned furniture views, a room placement inset, chair positions and internal item locations
2. One conversion and storage board tracing W-to-D conversion, all assembly IDs, the six work items and storage access paths
3. One two-page materials and connections sheet containing the assembly inventory, material assignments, fastener quantities, transformation joint and relocation joint
4. One relocation board containing the S1 starting position, separated modules, hardware pouch, packed work tote, two-adult holding positions and the complete doorway-to-corridor sequence

Acceptance:
- The W, D and S drawings show the same assembly IDs and quantities; W provides at least 1000 × 600 mm, D at least 1200 × 800 mm with two 600 × 400 mm place areas, both at 720–760 mm high, and S fits within 1100 × 600 × 850 mm.
- The three state drawings and relocation board preserve the 3600 × 3000 mm room, the 900 mm entrance strip, the fixed cabinet and window band, and the chair-parking coordinates in 01-client-facts.en.md; active chairs have 600 × 900 mm floor-use envelopes and clear associated leg space.
- The conversion and storage board traces L/K/M/N from the work surface into dimensioned internal compartments, with F/C already inside, and gives every assembly a location at every step; the board prints Work away, dinner ready and shows L closed before storage.
- The materials and connections sheet matches the state drawings' assembly IDs, quantities and dimensions, assigns 18 mm lacquered birch plywood and powder-coated steel tube to their specified components, and shows operation, support and retention for both joints, including the M6 relocation bolts and 4 mm hex key.
- The relocation board accounts for every furniture module and one hardware pouch, dimensions each module within 1300 × 850 × 250 mm, packs all six work items in the 400 × 320 × 180 mm tote, and shows their orientations through the 800 × 2050 mm doorway, 900 × 900 mm turn and rightward 900 mm-wide corridor.
- All five final images carry COMMONHOUR and their role or state in the title; the materials and connections sheet carries COMMONHOUR on its cover.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
